name: loose-realism-v1
description: Looser first touches, more wayward shooting, less-assisted/slower passing, slower & less perfect team-shape AI. Built 2026-08-23 from the decoded dt270 schema; semantics are name-based hypotheses until felt in-game.

edits.why: Bare global multiplier adjacent to ballControlWeekFootDownLimit; most likely scales the Ball Control attribute's contribution to the trap outcome (or the control success rate). Either reading: lower = worse first touch f

trapLoss=true is the master enable for heavy-touch ('loss') outcomes; trapLossDashOnly restricts them to sprint traps. Clearing the restriction lets walking/running traps also get away from the player — the most direct '

Ball-speed (kph) threshold at which a team-mate's ground pass is handled as a reflex 'reaction trap' rather than a clean trap, for a low-attribute player (paraMin). Normal grounders arrive at 32-36 kph (grounderpass.rece
High-attribute end of the same threshold (-15%). Top players still handle harder passes than weak ones, but the whole curve shifts down so more driven passes get the awkward handling.
Reaction time (s) for a low-attribute player on a fast team-mate ground pass. +33% = slower settle, ball bobbles/sits off the foot for an extra 3 frames. Longer time = worse under any reading.
High-attribute end of the reaction time (+30%), preserving the min/max ordering (0.20 > 0.13).

Same threshold for a BOUNCING ball (deflections, clearances, blocked shots) reaching a low-attribute player; -16% means more second balls are met with a reflex touch instead of a clean gather — directly 'loose balls happ
High-attribute end of the bouncing-ball threshold (-15%), keeps the min/max gap.

Reach-out trap: the player stretches to a ball that is not quite at the feet (enabled, up to reachOut.ballSpeed 50 kph). Reducing reach by 15% lets slightly off-line passes and deflections slip past instead of being hook

ballForceDirect (use=true) places the ball at a fixed offset ahead of the player after a trap: Idle 0.5 / Run 1.5 / Dash 2.0 (blendStartSpeed.speed_0/15/28 = 0.5/1.75/2.0 confirms these are distances growing with speed).
Same as above for sprint traps (+20%). Sprint first touches are where real players lose the ball most; this makes that the case here too.

After an unintended body collision, foot/leg/thigh cannot re-hit the ball for N frames (noHit.foot/reg/thigh all true). 10 -> 14 frames (+40%, ~67 ms more at 60 fps) keeps ricochets and blocked passes loose for longer be

BALL PHYSICS (separate from the trap edits): restitution per pitch condition. +10% makes every bounce livelier, so bouncing second balls are harder to gather and sit up for contests. Which of the six indices is live is c
Same +10% restitution, pitch-condition index 1.
Same +10% restitution, pitch-condition index 2.

Same +10% restitution for index 3, which is a distinct (heavier/wetter) surface with 0.5 base, frictionRollSpeedMax 50 and its own roll-back-spin rate; scaled proportionally so the surface stays relatively dead.
Same +10% restitution, pitch-condition index 4.
Same +10% restitution, pitch-condition index 5.

At max assist (index 3 = PA3) a long-held ground pass currently takes 0% of the stick direction. 0.2 blends a fifth of the aim into the target, so imprecise aiming produces under/over-hit or misdirected passes. Same dire
Short-press (weak gauge) ground passes at PA3 gain a small stick component; kept half the Strong value because short passes should stay mostly assisted (PA2 uses 0.3 vs 0.8).

Hypothesis: pass length (m) above which manual blending is applied (grounder 20, fly 30 fit metre ranges like manual.distForGageMin/Max 4..40). Lowering it subjects more medium-range passes to the stick blend.
Lofted equivalent of the grounder edit: PA3 strong-gauge lofted passes get 20% stick influence (PA1/PA2 already use 0.5).
Full-gauge lofted passes at PA3 also receive the stick blend (PA1/PA2 = 0.6). Leaves Weak.3 at 0 so short chips stay assisted.
Same hypothesis as the grounder threshold: lofted passes above ~22 m (instead of 30) become subject to the manual blend.

At PA3 a through ball is redirected to a runner from any angle (180). Narrowing to 120 means badly aimed through balls are no longer fully corrected and run through to nobody / the keeper — the classic 'wayward through b
PA2 equivalent: retarget cone shrinks ~27% so the stick must point closer to the runner. Keeps ordering PA1 (15) < PA2 (22) < PA3 (120).

Crosses at PA3 are currently aimed at a box target regardless of stick direction. 120 leaves a wide cone but lets a cross aimed well away from any teammate go where it was aimed. adjustSearchAngleRate/adjustStartPointRat

Only lever that scales pass quality by the passer's attribute for BOTH teams: a low-attribute passer's ground pass is hit at 78% speed instead of 90% (99-rated stays 1.0). Slower balls from weak passers fall short and ar

Weak lofted passers already loft max-distance balls higher than strong ones (6.3 vs 4.8). +19% adds hang time so their long balls are easier to contest/intercept and harder to bring down. Stays below heightForDistMax_hig

passget.defence maps a defensive attribute (paraMin 60 .. paraMax 90) to a timing 'sec' that is currently flat (0.4/0.4). Pattern-matching trap.reactionTrapBall.*.reactionTime suggests it is the defender's reaction delay

Launch elevation at full gauge for normal shots (28 == loop.angleY, so degrees). +18% moves the gauge fraction at which a shot from ~12 m clears the bar from roughly 36% to ~28% of the gauge (assuming near-linear interpo

Same lever for the finesse/control shot (+17%, matching the normal-shot ratio so the two types keep their relative feel). Control shots are the current meta for guaranteed corners-of-the-net placement; a higher ceiling m

Air-resistance multiplier (1.0 = Konami default). +12% bleeds more speed in flight, so shots from outside the box arrive weaker and dip more; close-range shots are barely affected because flight time is short — a natural

Magnus (curl) strength, +29%. More curl on any side-spun shot makes the ball deviate further from the aim line, producing more wayward finishes and more shots that curl past the post; the doc already notes 0.1 is absurd, [raised to 0.07 to amplify mishit sidespin — pairs with exe P1 slice unclamp]

Magnitude of the non-spin (knuckle) effect applied to balls in the nonSpinMin..nonSpinMax 45-105 kph window, which is exactly the shot-speed band. +30% makes hard, low-spin shots wobble more unpredictably — wayward for t

Chip-shot launch elevation in degrees. +4 deg makes chips hang higher and longer, giving the keeper more time to recover and sending over-hit chips over the bar, without changing the 40-80 kph speed window.

Distance-to-target-position beyond which an off-ball player in the defensive phase is forced to sprint (forceWalkDist 1.2 < forceJogDist 2.4 < forceDashDist 9 is a clear walk/jog/run/dash ladder). Raising it 33% means de
edits.inert: dead load in 0x143da92c0 — the defence branch uses 19-0.1*attr instead; only forceDashDistOffence is live

edits.why: Dead-zone: a player does not start moving to a new base position until it is this far from his current one. Raising 0.8 -> 1.2 m removes the constant micro-adjusting that makes AI shape look perfect and twitchy; players

Blend rate (0..1) of how strongly base positions are dragged toward uncovered space (paired with adjustSpaceCoverRate 0.23, coverRateZ 0.4, dfCoverEnable). Reducing by ~19% leaves more natural gaps between and inside lin

Rate (0..1) by which the collective base shape shifts toward the ball carrier, i.e. how much the whole unit 'presses' as a block. -20% yields a less swarming, less instant collective press while individual press decision
edits.inert: no reader found in the exe (docs/exe-gameplay-map.md)

edits.why: Prediction horizon (frames, 60 fps => 2.0 s) the positioning AI uses to anticipate where the play will be when choosing base positions (marginPredictionFrameBase is 0, so this is the whole horizon). Cutting to 1.5 s make

Duration (s) of the transition state after a possession change, during which shapes blend from attacking to defending (transitionSmooth 0, transitionOpenZ 1, transitionPriorityX 1 are its switches). Lengthening to 7 s ke

Percent chance/weight that a defender keeps his current match-up (man-marking assignment) instead of handing off to a teammate and snapping back to zonal shape. Raising by 10 points makes defenders follow runners further
Same as matchUpContinueRate but for FW/MF match-ups; keep the +10 offset Konami uses between the two so the relative behaviour of front and back units is preserved.

Threshold of an internal 'MF line urgency score' below which midfielders jog (walkMfLineScore 20 < jogMfLineScore 50 < run). Raising to 60 makes midfielders jog into position in more situations rather than run, slowing m

Front-to-back length of the defensive block in the Retreat state. Konami ships it identical to the normal lengthDf (35) with only SuperRetreat (30) distinct, so a retreating CPU looks the same as a normal one. Setting 32
